title: Security + KMS Intake — Axiom Therapeutics & Redwood
summary: First security posture intake for Axiom evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for inference. Primary concerns: KMS/BYOK, SOC2 evidence, SAML/SSO integration, RBAC model, audit log granularity, and data retention (PHI concerns / HIPAA). Agreed to share SOC2 report, security deck, and schedule infra deep-dive with customer's platform team next week.
topics: RBAC and permission model for multi-team access
Encryption: BYOK, HSM support, key rotation
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs: latency, cost, isolation
next_steps: Redwood to send SOC2 report and security whitepaper (Maya)
Schedule infra deep-dive with Ethan + Carlos for benchmarking (propose slots 2026-06-18/19)
Customer to provide list of regulated datasets and retention windows (Dr. Lena)
Follow-up on KMS BYOK architecture doc and HSM options (Ethan)

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-12 15:00 UTC | Duration 52m | Axiom Therapeutics intake: security, keys, hosting options
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Dr. Lena Ortiz (CISO), Carlos Mendez (Platform), Priya Singh (VP Eng)

Summary (auto): Quick intake to map security controls and gating criteria for inference. Focus on key management (BYOK/HSM), audit log fidelity, SSO and RBAC, and regulatory constraints (HIPAA/PHI).

00:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really quick intro — I'm Maya Chen, AE at Redwood. With me is Ethan Ross, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
00:29 Dr. Lena Ortiz: Hi Maya, thanks. We're good. We want to get straight to the sec stuff — we run clinical data pipelines so PHI is in scope and we need to understand how keys and logs are handled.
01:05 Maya: Totally, that's exactly why we set this up. Today we'll cover SOC2/ISO posture, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS. We'll also discuss Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private options that match your regulatory needs.
01:40 Carlos Mendez: Quick note: latency is important for interactive note-gen workflows in our clinician UI, but isolation and audit come first. We may trade a small latency delta if it closes the compliance gap.
02:05 Ethan (SE): Makes sense. A quick orientation: Redwood Hosted is our managed API with SOC2 and encrypted-at-rest defaults. Dedicated is reserved GPU pools with separate tenancy and optional VPC peering. Private gives you the control plane in your VPC or on-prem. BYOK and HSM options differ by mode.
02:40 Priya Singh: Can you expand BYOK? We have a corporate KMS and strict rotation policies, and any external system must use our keys.
03:05 Ethan: Yes — we support BYOK with AWS KMS and customer-managed keys. For Private, you can attach your HSM/KMS directly and we don't hold key material. For Dedicated we offer KMS proxies and a key-wrapping approach; it's not HSM-in-hosted but we can do envelope keys.
03:40 Dr. Lena Ortiz: So for Hosted, does Redwood ever have access to plaintext model inputs or keys? We need to ensure no key exfil and full separation.
04:05 Maya: Good question. In Hosted we manage the physical infra but keys can be customer-managed; we do not persist unencrypted material beyond retention windows you configure. For the highest guarantees we typically recommend Private (VPC) where customer controls the control plane and keys.
04:40 Speaker 2 (Carlos, paraphrase): There's often confusion in our security reviews around cached KV state and logs — does Redwood keep full request bodies in logs?
05:10 Ethan: By default audit logs capture metadata — request id, model, timestamp, token counts. We have configurable redaction rules for request/response bodies. Full payload logging is off by default for Hosted; for Dedicated/Private you control retention and what gets emitted to centralized logs.
05:45 Dr. Lena Ortiz: We need very fine-grained audit for HIPAA: user identity, what was requested, who accessed which model, and keystream rotation events. Can Redwood's logs show user id and role?
06:15 Ethan: Yes, we integrate with SSO (SAML/SCIM) so audit entries can include SAML assertion attributes like subject and groups. RBAC model maps groups to roles. We can include token-level mapping so logs show which API key or user initiated a call.
06:45 Maya: I'll note that SAML provisioning via SCIM is supported — most customers map Okta groups to Redwood roles. We also support session-level tracing for troubleshooting.
07:10 Priya Singh: How about retention — we have legal requirements to keep some telemetry for seven years but can't keep full content beyond 90 days. Is log retention customizable?
07:40 Ethan: Retention windows are customizable per deployment. Hosted tiers have standard retention buckets, but enterprise contracts for Dedicated/Private allow you to set retention policy and export logs to your SIEM or object store. You can also choose to redact or not log PII fields.
08:10 Dr. Lena Ortiz: SOC2 — do you have an up-to-date report and do you do penetration testing?
08:35 Maya: We have a current SOC2 Type II report and an ISO 27001 certification in process — we'll share the SOC2 report and our pen-test summary. We do regular pen tests and vulnerability scans and can provide an executive summary under NDA.
09:05 Carlos Mendez: For KMS rotation events, we want to see key usage audit events — who rotated, when, which systems used the key. Is that surfaced?
09:30 Ethan: Yes — KMS audit events are surfaced if you use your KMS and export CloudTrail/HSM logs into your account. For Dedicated where Redwood intermediates keys we can surface rotation events in audit logs and tie them to user ids, though the highest fidelity is when keys live in your account.
10:00 (short crosstalk)
10:25 Priya Singh: Private on-prem sounds like the cleanest approach for us but that has cost and ops overhead. Can you run Redwood Private in our K8s cluster behind airgap?
10:55 Ethan: Yes, we have an on-prem package that can run in air-gapped clusters. It supports customer KMS (HSM) integrations and local logging to your SIEM. We're used to a deployment checklist: network, NFS/obj store, and a small ops runbook.
11:30 Dr. Lena Ortiz: We also need RBAC to isolate product teams — clinical vs research vs analytics. Each team should only have access to their model endpoints and logs.
11:55 Ethan: Our RBAC supports role-based policies and per-model route permissions. You can bind Okta groups or SAML attributes to roles and enforce per-route write/read. We also support per-token cost attribution for billing.
12:25 Maya: Do you have any hard cutoffs or gating criteria for going to production with PHI?
12:50 Dr. Lena Ortiz: Internal policy: PHI workloads must be on customer-controlled keys and isolated network. So target is Private or Dedicated with customer-managed keys. Hosted is a maybe if keys never leave our account and logs export to our SIEM.
13:20 Carlos Mendez: About network — can Dedicated use VPC peering with our account and we block internet egress?
13:45 Ethan: Yes, Dedicated can be peered and you can restrict egress. Private gives you full network control. For Hosted we have region controls and private connectivity options (VPN or private link) but not full peering in standard hosted.
14:10 (brief pause)
14:25 Priya Singh: Any third-party sub processors? We need list for vendor review.
14:45 Maya: We'll send a current vendor/subprocessor list in the security pack along with SOC2.
15:10 Dr. Lena Ortiz: About encryption at rest — are model weights encrypted in your storage? Are caches encrypted?
15:35 Ethan: Yes, at-rest storage is encrypted. For KV caches and model checkpoints we use disk-level encryption with customer-managed KMS where possible. For Private, you own the key. For Dedicated we support envelope encryption where master keys are in your account.
16:05 Carlos Mendez: Can we rotate keys monthly? Our policy mandates 30-day rotation for some keys.
16:30 Ethan: We support rotation schedules; for BYOK we recommend rotation with careful rewrap so inference isn't disrupted. There is an operational window for cache warmup after rotation, we can run planned rotations with minimal impact.
17:00 (unintelligible)
17:20 Dr. Lena Ortiz: Do you maintain immutable audit logs with tamper evidence? We need to show chain of custody.
17:45 Ethan: We can ship logs to your immutable store (S3 with WriteOnce policies or third-party WORM storage). Redwood's internal logs are append-only and we keep hash chaining for critical events if required under enterprise contract.
18:10 Maya: Does Redwood offer SOC2 attestation for dedicated/private customers as part of contract?
18:35 Maya: We provide SOC2 artifacts and can include contract language around audit support. For Private, customer-side controls will be primary.
19:00 Priya Singh: What about personnel access? Can we limit Redwood support engineers' access to production models?
19:25 Ethan: Yes — we have RBAC for internal ops. You can require justification and time-limited access (just-in-time) and we log access approvals. We also support session recording for privileged ops.
19:55 Dr. Lena Ortiz: We will need SSO (Okta) — how fast to onboard via SAML/SCIM?
20:20 Maya: Typical is 48–72 hours once we get SAML metadata and SCIM mapping details. We can do an initial test app and push to a pilot group.
20:50 Carlos Mendez: For the bench tests, we want to run a spike to measure p99 latency for our average token lengths and peak throughput. What do you need from us?
21:10 Ethan: Sample payloads and a test account. We'll provision a Dedicated trial pool or do an in-account Private staging. Ideally provide concurrency profile and sequence length distribution. We'll run benchmarks and share a spreadsheet.
21:45 Priya Singh: Pricing question quickly — how does Dedicated billing differ for reserved capacity vs burst? Could burst cross our budget guardrails?
22:10 Maya: Dedicated is reserved with burst capacity add-ons on top. We can set guardrails and alert thresholds; cost attribution per team helps keep budgets visible. We'll send the pricing sheet but final structuring often happens during procurement.
22:40 Dr. Lena Ortiz: Any known compliance gaps for HIPAA workflows we should flag?
22:55 Ethan: HIPAA posture is fine for Private deployments. Hosted can meet HIPAA under BAAs with certain config — e.g., BYOK and log export. We'll surface specifics in the security pack.
23:20 (brief pause)
23:40 Maya: Ok let's recap next steps — we'll send SOC2, subprocessor list, and security deck. Ethan will prepare BYOK/HSM notes and bench plan. Your team to share PHI data points and retention windows.
24:05 Dr. Lena Ortiz: Sounds good. Timeline: we want to decide by end of Q3 and run a pilot in July.
24:25 Carlos Mendez: We'll try to get sample payloads by next Thursday.
24:40 Ethan: I'll propose two deep-dive slots for the infra benchmark — 6/18 and 6/19.
24:55 Priya Singh: One more — can you share a short example of audit log schema?
25:20 Ethan: Yes, I'll attach an example JSON schema in the follow-up. It includes event_type, user_id, role, model, route, token_counts, request_hash (optional), and retention metadata.
25:45 (overlap)
26:00 Dr. Lena Ortiz: A couple of red flags from our side — if Hosted requires Redwood-managed keys without BYOK, that's a blocker. Also if logs can't be exported to our SIEM we need to re-evaluate.
26:25 Maya: Understood. We'll make those high-priority items in the security pack.
26:50 Carlos Mendez: For procurement, what's the SLA for Dedicated?
27:10 Maya: Dedicated has an SLA in enterprise contracts, typically uptime + latency windows; we'll share the SLA and the runbook for incident response.
27:35 Priya Singh: Can you show how you handle model rollouts and rollback auditing? We need to know when a model variant replaced another and who approved it.
27:55 Ethan: Rollouts are tracked in the control plane with audit trails: who triggered, which artifact hash, and rollout percentage. We emit events into audit logs and can integrate with your CI/CD approvals.
28:25 Dr. Lena Ortiz: That helps. Any final questions from Redwood side?
28:45 Maya: No, just that we'll follow up quickly.
29:00 (closing chatter — logistics)
29:20 Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll email the security pack and proposed times.
29:30 Dr. Lena Ortiz: Thank you.
29:35 (meeting ends)

Notes: Transcript contains occasional mis-hearings and speaker label inconsistencies typical of Fireflies exports — some timestamps are approximate. Shared artifacts mentioned: redwood-security-pack.pdf, SOC2-report (NDA), KMS-byok-architecture.pdf, audit-log-schema.json, dedicated-pricing-sheet.xlsx.
